newsitem.title: UK: US stocks narrowly mixed in London after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: US stocks narrowly mixed in London after rate hike.

text.p: U.S. stocks were narrowly mixed in thin dealings in London on Wednesday as markets digested the first U.S. rate hike in more than two years, dealers said.
"Now the question is, is this the first in a series?" said one dealer. Wall Street is likely to consolidate now as the market mulls the possibility, he added.
Most activity in London focused on shares in AT&T Corp, which goes ex-dividend today. The shares were down $1/4 from their New York closing level at $35-3/4, which is expected to weigh on the Dow.
"It's strictly an ex-dividend play," said another dealer of the decline in AT&T shares.

Shares in Boeing Co eased $3/4 to $103-3/4 in London on news that the relatives of several victims of a 1991 plane crash in Colorado are suing the aircraft manufacturer and United Airlines UAL.L, dealers said.
The suit alleges that mishandling of the wreckage from the plane has deprived the relatives of evidence they would need to help prove their claim that the crash was caused by a faulty rudder.
"The story spooked a few people," the dealer said. "People are very jumpy about it."
Dealings were spotty elsewhere, they said. Shares in General Motors Corp were up $1/8 to $57-1/8, while shares in Ford Motor Co climbed $1/4 to $32. Chrysler Corp shares were unchanged at $30-5/8.
Technology shares were mixed, with Intel Corp rising $1/4 to $133-1/2 and shares in International Business Machines Corp slipped $1/8 to $136.
In other trading, June S&P 500 index futures advanced 0.60 point ti 795.80 on Globex at 1129 GMT, while June long bond futures were unchanged at 108-23/32.
London dealers were expecting Wall Street to open firmer, although the market's direction would likely be influenced by data on orders for durable goods for February, due for release at 1330 GMT.
"As long as the (long) bond yield holds below seven percent, I think there's scope for Wall Street to move a bit higher," the dealer added.
